newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso checks early slide at close.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso checks early slide at close.

text.p: The Mexican peso checked an early speculative run to close across the board at slightly less than eight per dollar on Monday.
Traders said the peso recovered as dealers who had overbought dollars in the morning stepped in to sell them in the afternoon, and when some foreign capital trickled back into Mexico.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both ended 4.9 weaker, respectively, at 7.9875/7.9950 and 7.9840/7.9940 per dollar.
"The market was very odd. First the peso plummeted, and then it rebounded," a trader said.
"Some dealers certainly overbought and then dollars flowed back litle by little. Some foreign investors stepped in, albeit very few," he added.
Dealers said forecasts for sharp increases in primary interest rates at Tuesday's central bank auction bolstered the peso in late trade.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier two centavos weaker at 7.9790/7.9850 per dollar.
"I feel the peso still has plenty of scope to fall over the coming days, but much depends on the outcome of the Cetes auction," another trader said.
Traders said they predicted increases of up to 300 basis points for bellwether 28-day Cetes rates, and an average of 100 basis points for longer-term issues.
"The market well withstood the peso closing at below eight pesos per dollar. Let's see how it fares at the open tomorrow," a dealer said.
Traders situated support for the 48-hour peso at 8.00 per dollar, and a second support at 8.03 per dollar.
